task: Redesign the round-01 convergence evidence figure into a clearer Nature-first research figure while keeping the supplied practice data and scientific meaning fixed.
title: Displayed trajectories decrease overall; Proposed has one temporary increase at iteration 6
data_source: examples/data/convergence_practice.csv, carried forward unchanged from round 01
objective: Show the observed objective trajectories and make the one local non-monotone update visible without implying unsupported speed, stability, or statistical superiority.
core_conclusion: Within the displayed illustrative trajectories, all three methods end below their displayed starting values; the Proposed trace ends at the lowest shown objective, while its only positive step is visible as a local deviation from its running best at iteration 6.
claim: Within the displayed illustrative trajectories, all three methods end below their displayed starting values; the Proposed trace ends at the lowest shown objective, while its only positive step is visible as a local deviation from its running best at iteration 6.
audience: Readers of a mathematical modelling or algorithm research paper

canvas.intended_placement: double-column figure; single-column preview is a stress test rather than the target placement

layout.label: a
layout.content: Raw current objective for all three algorithms across iterations 1–10, with direct endpoint labels and a local current-versus-incumbent callout at Proposed iteration 6.

layout.label: b
layout.content: Signed adjacent-step objective changes on the same iteration scale; a zero reference makes the positive Proposed step explicit.

evidence_panels.question: How do the observed objective values evolve, and where does current differ from the running best?
Which adjacent updates decrease or increase the objective under minimization?

encoding.algorithm: consistent restrained color plus marker shape across panels
encoding.historical_best: shown only at the single Proposed point where it differs from current; other historical-best values coincide with current and are not redundantly overplotted
encoding.delta_objective: signed y-position relative to a zero reference
encoding.direction: lower objective is better; negative delta is a decrease

uncertainty.reason: The input has one deterministic practice trajectory per algorithm and no replicate or error estimate.

design_decisions: Removed the first-round endpoint dumbbell because it repeated the trajectory endpoints without adding a distinct evidence layer.
Replaced the first-round heatmap with a signed update strip to avoid a colorbar and dense cell-by-cell interpretation.
Used one figure-level conclusion sentence and direct endpoint labels instead of multiple competing titles and legends.
Kept the first-round data, objective direction, colors, and Nature skill version fixed for controlled comparison.
limitations: This practice dataset cannot support general algorithm performance claims.
A single-column placement is likely to reduce text and marker legibility; double-column width is the intended use for this information density.
No convergence threshold or stability metric is asserted because none is specified by the input.
review_risks: The single trajectory per algorithm cannot support uncertainty or statistical claims.
The label Proposed must not be interpreted as validated superiority.
The signed delta convention must remain explicit because the objective is minimized.
The double-column placement is the intended target; the single-column render is a readability stress test.
scientific_unknowns: No repeated runs, seeds, benchmark context, or real-unit interpretation are provided.
No stopping criterion or target threshold is defined.
The table does not establish performance outside the displayed ten iterations.
user_reference_note: No personal figure-gallery image was used or modified for this controlled comparison.
